items.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.summary: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
items.content:
It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news.

Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor, pouring tens of billions into startups annually, and participating in 105 rounds this year alone often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital.

Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition.

“Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamilla Bankiya told TechCrunch.

Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term.

Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress is expected to institute some changes , especially when it comes to Nvidia’s investments into AI startups at the crux of the billion-dollar data centre build-out . Huang’s rampant dealmaking in this sphere has been a source of concern for Wall Street.

“She’s much more conservative,” one investor said of Kress. “I don’t think she’s going to commit the same amount of money to keep the early-stage ecosystem going.”

Nvidia’s biggest bets were backing neoclouds, inference providers, and open weight models, which are expensive for smaller companies to build. “Jensen’s initiatives are a big reason an ecosystem has emerged despite that,” Zain Javid, co-founder of the hardware company Ghost, said.

For instance, Nvidia backed CoreWeave back when it was still private, and participated in two of Crusoe’ rounds, including its $1.4 billion Series E. It bought Hugging Face this year for $13 billion (expected to close in 2027) and holds investments in Mistral AI, Lambda, and Black Forest Labs. Nvidia was often the largest investor in the deals. Last year, it wrote an $800 million check into a $2 billion Series B round for Reflection AI, before the open-source startup began to earn meaningful revenue, according to the Wall Street Journal .

“Jensen believed in open source and frankly speaking, Europe,” Bankiya said of how Huang invested so much in AI across the world. The cease of that support in other regions outside of America, like Europe “would be a massive funding and honestly ecosystem gap that no one can fill.”

It’s also true that Nvidia was such a dominant player in the ecosystem that at times, it felt like a monopoly. By backing so many companies with such generous checks, Nvidia effectively locked those startups into using its chips which helped reinforce its dominant market position.

If the company does grow more conservative with its startup investments, that could leave more room for rivals and smaller competitors. (Coincidentally, Google announced two new chips this week amid Huang’s Nvidia fallout).

Some investors with whom TechCrunch spoke hope that large cloud companies and other chipmakers will step in to back startups and fill some of the void that will likely be left by Huang.

Dharmesh Thakker, a general partner at Battery Ventures, for example, expects big tech rivals to vie for Nvidia’s investment crown, “depending upon who brings the best combination of a great product, an ecosystem and community to compete with CUDA, and the financial power to bankroll the ecosystem,” he said. CUDA is Nvidia’s software platform that enables developers to run AI models on its GPUs.

While companies like Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and AMD may back mature startups to drive adoption of their chips and clouds, Thakker doubts they will pour hundreds of millions into pre-revenue infrastructure startups the way Nvidia did.

Under Huang, infrastructure companies that needed $100 million to $500 million in GPUs would often raise half of that amount at valuations of $1 billion or more from Nvidia just to get started, one VC said. The chipmaker’s participation gave other investors the comfort in backing these companies at the lofty valuations.

Now, Nvidia is expected to be more selective in the new companies it backs, while writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio, contributing to a drop in valuations.

“When Nvidia was on the cap table, everyone felt safe,” Padval said. Without that backing, investors say traditional VCs are likely to think twice before writing checks into these startups and may even pause certain dealmaking.

Even so, few believe that Nvidia’s investment slowdown will by itself halt the broader AI boom.

Though everyone agrees that Huang is a massive loss for Nvidia, one of his ex-employees, Amulya Vishwanath, who now runs her own VC fund, said that “founders and leaders must be held accountable,” and that the ecosystem is bigger than one person. “That talent will, and must, continue to thrive.”

items.content:
Black Friday is still weeks away, but early Black Friday deals on some of our favorite tech are already rolling in, including Apple’s AirPods. Both the flagship AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2 are on sale, knocking up to $100 off their regular prices. Whether you want pocketable earbuds for everyday use, premium noise-canceling headphones, or seamless Apple integration, these are some of the best prices I've seen recently. I don't expect these prices to go back up until after Black Friday, but with tech getting more expensive , I wouldn't wait too long if you've been planning to upgrade.

For headphone recommendations, check out our guides to the Best Wireless Earbuds , the Best Open Earbuds , and the Best Headphones for Working Out .

The flagship AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s best AirPods yet. Upgrades include stronger noise-canceling, a new acoustic architecture for deeper bass, and redesigned ear tips for a more secure fit. The ear tips also keep my AirPods from slipping during longer runs and sweatier workouts. New tools include a built-in heart rate sensor for fitness tracking, live translation, and a camera remote to snap photos or videos on your iPhone. These earbuds are also the first AirPods to be IP57 rated against dust, sweat, and rain.

Right now, they are 20 percent off at Amazon , Target , and Walmart . There’s no telling if these discounts will change once Black Friday is here, so I’d grab a pair now if they’re on your wish list.

The AirPods Max 2 ’s newer H2 chip improves active noise cancellation and transparency mode and enables a suite of intelligent features, including conversation awareness, live translation, and improved Siri interactions. The AirPods Max 2 are designed with a new high-dynamic-range amplifier for deeper bass, more natural vocals, and cleaner highs. The ear cuffs, while plush and comfortable for longer listening sessions, do trap some heat, but I have yet to find a pair of over-ear headphones that don’t.

At $549, the AirPods Max 2 can be a tough sell, especially with so many excellent, more affordable alternatives on the market. But $100 off, they’re a lot easier to justify, especially if you want the seamless integration that comes with Apple’s ecosystem.

items.content:
젠슨 황의 퇴임이 엔비디아를 넘어 AI 산업 전체에 충격을 주고 있습니다. 세계 AI 반도체 시장을 지배하는 기업의 창업자가 물러났다는 사실보다, 지난 수년간 막대한 자금과 영향력을 동원해 AI 산업의 성장을 이끌어 온 핵심 인물이 사라졌다는 점이 주목됩니다.

가장 큰 관심은 엔비디아의 공격적인 투자 전략이 유지될지입니다. 이 회사는 최근 'AI의 은행'으로 불릴 만큼 반도체 공급을 넘어 AI 산업의 주요 자금줄로 자리 잡았습니다. 오픈AI에 300억달러를 투자하고 오픈AI 관련 데이터센터 사업의 임대·개발 의무에 대해 최대 1050억달러의 조건부 보증을 제공하기로 하는 등 핵심 후원자 역할을 해왔습니다. 앤트로픽의 기업공개(IPO)에도 100억달러를 투자하기로 했습니다. AI 모델 개발사부터 코어위브·네비우스 같은 네오클라우드 업체, 미디어텍 등 반도체·장비 관련 기업까지 투자 대상도 광범위합니다.

로이터 에 따르면 엔비디아의 재무상 약정 규모는 1645억달러(약 220조원)에 달합니다. 지난 8월에는 블랙록 등 6개 금융사와 함께 AI 인프라 구축을 위해 5000억달러 이상의 외부 자금을 조달하는 계획도 발표했습니다. 이 가운데 최대 1250억달러를 지원할 수 있다고 밝혔습니다. AI 산업에 투자해 반도체 수요를 키우고, 여기서 얻은 수익을 다시 산업에 투입하는 구조를 구축한 것입니다.

이런 전략은 황 전 CEO가 직접 주도해 왔습니다. 그는 투자 대상 스타트업의 기술 개발에 관여하고 고객사를 연결해 주는 것은 물론, 투자 유치를 위한 전화 회의에도 직접 참여했습니다. 단순히 자금을 집행하는 경영자를 넘어 AI 산업의 사업 관계를 직접 구축한 셈입니다.

차기 경영진이 막대한 재정 부담과 투자 위험을 감수하면서까지 이런 전략을 이어갈지는 불확실합니다. 당장 앤트로픽 IPO 투자 약속과 130억달러 규모로 추진 중인 허깅페이스 인수 등 대형 거래가 시험대에 올랐습니다.

전략이 바뀐다면 그 영향은 AI 산업 전체로 이어질 수 있습니다. 그동안 엔비디아의 투자와 신용 지원을 통해 자금을 조달하고 데이터센터를 확장해 온 기업들은 새로운 투자자를 찾아야 할 수도 있습니다. 최근에는 AI 인프라에 투입되는 막대한 자금과 부채에 대한 경계심이 커진 상황이라, 어려움이 가중될 수 있습니다.

아시아 반도체 공급망에도 변화가 예상됩니다. 황 전 CEO는 TSMC와 SK하이닉스, 삼성전자 등 주요 협력사 경영진을 직접 만나 생산능력 확대와 차세대 기술 개발을 독려해 왔습니다. 로이터 에 따르면 대만 공급업계에서는 새 CEO가 황 전 CEO만큼 공격적으로 생산능력을 확보하지 않을 수 있다는 관측이 나옵니다. 한국에서도 SK그룹과 추진하는 대규모 AI 인프라 협력과 네이버 등 국내 기업과의 사업 관계가 새로운 경영진 아래에서 어떻게 이어질지 주목하고 있습니다.

미·중 AI 패권 경쟁은 물론, 글로벌 AI 반도체 시장의 경쟁 구도에도 영향을 줄 수 있습니다. 비즈니스 인사이더 에 따르면 번스타인 리서치의 스테이시 라스곤은 황 전 CEO를 '미국 AI 발전 방향의 설계자'로 평가하며, 그의 퇴임으로 가장 큰 이익을 얻는 쪽은 중국이 될 것이라고 주장했습니다. 엔비디아의 경영 공백이 길어지면 중국 반도체 기업들이 기술 격차를 좁힐 기회를 얻을 수 있다는 것입니다.

AMD와 브로드컴 등 미국 경쟁사에도 시장점유율을 확대할 기회가 생길 수 있습니다. 실제로 황 전 CEO의 퇴임 소식 이후 엔비디아와 주요 고객사 주가는 하락한 데 비해 AMD와 브로드컴, 중국 주요 GPU 기업들의 주가는 상승했습니다.

중국에 대한 미국 정부의 정책은 오히려 강경해질 가능성이 있습니다. 황 전 CEO는 트럼프 대통령과 긴밀한 관계를 구축하고 중국 시장의 중요성을 강조하며 반도체 수출 규제 완화를 적극 주장해 왔습니다. 하지만 중국 스파이 의혹에 연루되면서 오히려 대중국 수출 규제 강화를 주장하는 정치권에 힘을 실어준 셈입니다.

실제로 마이크 존슨 미국 하원의장 은 12일 중국에 대한 반도체 수출 제한에 의회 내 공감대가 형성되고 있다고 밝혔습니다. 황 전 CEO를 둘러싼 논란을 계기로 그동안 수출 규제 강화를 요구해 온 정치권의 목소리가 커지면서, 중국 AI 기업들의 첨단 GPU 접근이 더 어려워질 수 있습니다. 중국 입장에서는 엔비디아의 경영 혼란이 기회이면서 동시에 새로운 위험이 된 것입니다.

오픈웨이트 AI 생태계도 영향을 받을 수 있습니다. 황 전 CEO는 '네모트론' 모델 개발과 오픈웨이트 AI 지원을 주도하고 미국 정부의 과도한 규제에도 반대해 왔습니다. 허깅페이스 인수를 추진하고 리플렉션 AI 등 미국 오픈 모델 기업에도 투자했습니다.

특히 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등 폐쇄형 모델 업체들이 미국 정부에 규제 강화를 요청했을 때는 다른 기술 기업들을 결집해 공개적으로 반대 의견을 제시하기도 했습니다. 테크크런치 는 그의 퇴임으로 미국 오픈 모델 진영이 가장 강력한 후원자 중 한 명을 잃었다고 평가했습니다. 물론 회사 내부에서는 네모트론 개발에 변화가 없을 것이라는 전망도 나옵니다.

엔비디아의 기술 경쟁력이 당장 무너질 가능성은 크지 않습니다. 향후 1~2년간 출시할 제품은 이미 개발과 생산이 진행 중이며, 주요 고객사의 투자 계획도 단기간에 바뀌지는 않을 것으로 예상됩니다.

그러나 황 전 CEO는 반도체 개발부터 투자와 금융 지원, 공급망 협력, 미국 정부와의 관계까지 사실상 AI 산업의 여러 축을 직접 연결해 왔습니다. 그가 없는 엔비디아가 앞으로도 'AI의 은행'이자 산업 전체의 성장 동력으로 남을 수 있을지, 아니면 수익성과 위험 관리에 집중하는 반도체 기업으로 돌아갈지가 AI 산업의 다음 국면을 결정할 핵심 변수로 떠올랐습니다.

■ 구글·삼성, AI 안경 시장 출사표… 12월10일 메타와 정식 격돌

구글과 삼성전자가 제미나이를 탑재한 AI 안경을 12월10일 출시하며 메타가 주도해 온 시장에 도전장을 내밀었습니다. 메타 AI 안경의 국내 판매 실적이 아직 알려지지 않은 가운데, 이 제품이 국내 AI 안경 시장에서 새로운 수요를 만들어낼 수 있을지 주목됩니다.

■ 구글, 판단 전용 AI '제미나이 디시전 1' 출시...질문 1000개 동시 처리

뒤늦게 판단 전용 AI 시장에 뛰어든 구글이 자체 평가에서 경쟁 모델을 앞선 성능과 저렴한 가격을 내세웠습니다. 특히 이미지·음성·영상까지 직접 처리하는 멀티모달 기술이 제품의 경쟁력으로 이어질지 주목됩니다.

■ 알리바바, '큐원4' 첫 모델 공개…가중치·성능 평가 없이 프리뷰 출시

알리바바가 차세대 AI 모델 '큐원4' 시리즈의 첫 주자를 선보였습니다. 그러나 모델 가중치와 벤치마크 결과를 공개하지 않고 2주간 제한적으로 제공해, 실제 성능과 기존 오픈웨이트 전략의 변화 여부에 관심이 모입니다.

items.title: US government grounds all flights across the United States ‘due to extraordinary circumstances’
items.summary: A spokesperson for the FAA told TechCrunch that it issued the ground stop "following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers," which manage the airspace across the United States.
items.content:
The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday afternoon that it has grounded all flights across the United States due to “extraordinary circumstances” and issues related to safety.

The FAA’s website said the cause is an “equipment outage.” The site itself was down for a brief period at the time of publication, with a note that the website was “experiencing technical difficulties.”

Per an alert sent by the Air Traffic Control System Command Center , or ATCSCC, the FAA said the ground stop means that aircraft cannot take off from departure gates. The message said that the disruption was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” but did not specify further. The alert was not visible on the ATCSCC website at press time.

The alert stated that all departing flights must remain on the ground “until further notice.” Inbound international flights will be “managed on a case-by-case basis,” it said.

A spokesperson for the FAA told TechCrunch that it issued the ground stop “following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” which manage the airspace across the United States.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X : “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”

It’s not clear what caused the ongoing FAA equipment outage. The outage comes in the same week that the administration rolled out an AI-powered tool for air traffic controllers to save aircraft flight time and fuel costs — though it’s unclear if the ongoing outage is related.

Speaking to reporters outside the White House, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that there is “no indication yet that this was a nefarious act,” but warned that the recovery “is going to take some time.”

items.title: FAA Grounds All US Flights Until Further Notice
items.summary: The government cited a nationwide communications failure among air traffic control systems as the reason for the sudden grounding on Friday.
items.content:
The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all US flights Friday afternoon, due to “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the agency said in a statement. Flights already in the air will be allowed to land, the agency said, but no new ones are permitted to take off.

In a post on X , US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the ground stop was related to a communication issue affecting Air Traffic Control Centers, and said that agency technicians are investigating.

The ground stop came after widespread reports of radio frequency outages among several of the nation’s most critical Air Traffic Control Centers, including in Boston, Chicago, and New York. Air traffic controllers use designated radio frequencies to communicate with pilots and manage and monitor airspace safety. In the past, controllers have used voice communications relayed over these radio frequencies to direct traffic; in recent years, the FAA has also rolled out a text-based communication system .

Reached for comment, an FAA spokesperson did not provide any additional details.

Nationwide ground stops are rare. The FAA halted all air traffic on September 11, 2001. In January of 2023, a ground stop was issued after an outage to a critical system that the FAA used to distribute real-time data and warnings to pilots, known as NOTAM (Notice to Air Mission).

“This really points to how much we need to modernize our air traffic control system,” says Susan Hotle, a professor of transportation engineering at Virginia Tech who worked at the FAA. “Right now all it takes is for one system to go out, and it affects a wide region at once.”

Earlier Friday, Duffy wrote congressional leaders to ask lawmakers to “act swiftly” on the Transportation Department’s request for $30.1 billion funding updates to the nation’s air traffic control system.

If the outage lasts more than a couple hours, it will take airlines—and the flyers that depend on them—days to recover, says Michael McCormick, a professor at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University and a former air traffic controller. An extended stop would mean “airline systems are going to be complete in chaos, with aircraft and air crews in the wrong places. It would take days to get up and back running normally,” he says.

The FAA said this week that it was rolling out a new AI tool to help advise air traffic controllers. The tool, now available nationwide, had been tested in the busy Washington, DC, region. There is no evidence to suggest today’s ground stop is related to this new tool.

At San Francisco International Airport on Friday, hoards of confused travelers lined up to speak with airline staff. A number flights at the airport had already been delayed because of high winds, and the FAA ground stop was now compounding the issue.

“The FAA has issued a nationwide ground stop,” a United Airlines employee said over the intercom at Terminal 3 near the E departure gates. “This is a nationwide event.”

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates . Louise Matsakis contributed reporting.

items.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
items.summary: Airlines praised the AI tool, but the air traffic controllers’ union wasn’t involved.
items.content:
The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment.

“After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.

The FAA fact sheet describes SMART as a cloud-based system that combines information about “weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics” to predict air traffic patterns. It is designed to make scheduling recommendations, identify optimal flight routes, and determine the best order of arrivals for aircraft.

However, a human team of FAA specialists based in DC is ultimately responsible for validating the SMART system recommendations before passing them along to air traffic control facilities across the country, according to the agency.

Furthermore, the AI-powered SMART system “cannot be used to replace the critical role air traffic controllers play or take over control of an aircraft,” the FAA clarified in the September 21 announcement about the initial deployment. Local air traffic controllers can decide whether or not to accept the SMART system recommendations.

The previous FAA announcement included supportive statements from Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian and American Airlines CEO Robert Isom.

But the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, which represents more than 15,000 members, also told Flying magazine that it was not consulted or involved in the “design, testing, or implementation of SMART and therefore cannot speak to its effect on the air traffic control workforce.”

Following the initial deployment in airspace above DC, the FAA expanded the SMART system’s coverage to air route traffic control centers in Atlanta along with Jacksonville and Miami in Florida, according to The Dallas Morning News .

The FAA also shared an example with The Dallas Morning News about how SMART recommended a shorter and faster route for a cargo flight arriving at Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, although the newspaper noted that the agency did not identify the flight involved and has not provided information about how SMART may have assisted passenger flight traffic.

Ars has previously covered the SMART system’s development and lingering questions about how it works, as well as the air traffic controller shortage and other challenges facing the FAA.

items.content:
OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents.﻿

After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they’ll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI’s support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan.

After you review the AI agent’s purchase and sign off on it, OpenAI says that, similar to using tap to pay , Apple Pay , or Google Wallet , it substitutes your credit card details with a payment token, so your actual card info isn’t shared with your Dots agent or the business you’re buying from. Eventually, OpenAI says it expects “users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters—such as spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods—and pre-approve those purchases.”

ChatGPT Wallet might not work everywhere. Some retailers have restrictions on AI agents or block them altogether. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents. OpenAI says that in order for agents to use ChatGPT Wallet, “websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.”

items.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.summary: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.
items.content:
Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday.

That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago , led by IVP.

LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence.

With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs. It also promises that LangSmith will contain agent behavior and is easy to use.

True, there are plenty of other startups pitching similar advantages these days and also doing well ( case in point is newcomer Mintive ). However, LangChain has had a head start and now claims 7,000 LangSmith customers, including big-name startups like Harvey, Rippling, and Clay, and enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
items.summary: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash.
items.content:
Sorry, Margaret, your email is working again.

After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page .

The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

The full cause of Microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

“We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” a Microsoft spokesperson says in a statement. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.”

The company has promised a “full post-incident report” after it has fully reviewed what went wrong.

As Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and other Microsoft 365 systems come back online, users will likely see their inboxes turn into a mess. “You're probably going to get a lot of notifications when things come back,” says Jonathan Leitschuh, an independent researcher.

Microsoft said it had increased the queue time for emails to 48 hours in an attempt to ensure that every message that people tried to send while its systems were down gets delivered. Leitschuh points out that, even with the bulk of systems restored, users may receive “a flood of notifications a few hours down the pike” as subsystems come back online.

The total impact of the Microsoft outage may never be fully known, but it’s safe to say it’s already significant. Governments from Japan to the United States reported disruptions to a bevy of functions. Airlines reported problems with their ability to communicate with customers. Many law enforcement and emergency services ground to a halt . And hospitals reported widespread interruptions to their operations.

Ultimately, the episode serves as a reminder of the risks involved when the whole world relies on a single company for a critical service . “We're very interdependent on these systems in modern life,” says Leitschuh. Next time, delayed emails may be the least of our worries.

items.title: $11.4M in Nvidia hardware vanishes during shipment from CA to TX
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.freightwaves.com/news/11-4-million-in-nvidia-hardware-vanishes-during-shipment-from-california-to-texas Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50487864 Points: 228 # Comments: 126
items.content:
Six pallets of NVIDIA computer hardware worth a reported $11.4 million disappeared during a shipment from California to Texas. A truck collected the merchandise in Oakland on Aug. 29 for delivery to Fort Worth. Investigators reportedly tracked the vehicle through several extended stops before losing its trail in Southern California. The Oakland Police Department confirmed an ongoing grand theft investigation following a complaint filed Sept. 13, 2026. The disappearance comes amid reports of nearly $111 million in stolen data center freight involving other high-value technology shipments.

According to The Mercury News , the vehicle displayed a food transportation company’s logo during the scheduled pickup. The driver subsequently traveled south, making several stops lasting multiple hours. Investigators eventually lost track of the truck in San Bernardino County. A separate $12 million cargo theft investigation involved suspects who allegedly exploited established trucking identities to obtain freight. Authorities have not linked the two investigations.

The Oakland Police Department provided FreightWaves with the following statement:

“The Oakland Police Department (OPD) is investigating a grand theft that occurred in East Oakland. The victim reported the crime to OPD on September 13, 2026. The investigation is ongoing, and anyone with information is asked to contact the OPD General Crimes Unit at (510) 238-3728.”

The Sept. 13 complaint date does not establish when the theft occurred. Police have not confirmed the reported $11.4 million valuation or identified the specific merchandise. Authorities also have not identified the cargo’s owner, shipper, motor carrier or driver. Investigators have not publicly explained the vehicle’s extended stops or established whether criminals impersonated a transportation provider. Police have not announced arrests or confirmed any recovery of the merchandise. FreightWaves contacted NVIDIA for comment and followed up, but the company has not responded.

The Oakland investigation follows other significant thefts involving NVIDIA merchandise in Northern California. During 2025, Fremont and Union City police investigated burglaries involving more than $7.5 million in NVIDIA products. Those incidents targeted valuable computer hardware at separate locations. Authorities have not established any connection between those investigations and the latest disappearance.

In a separate September incident, thieves stole two PlusAI trailers, including one displaying NVIDIA branding , from a Fremont, California, warehouse. The trailers contained approximately 40,000 pounds of sand rather than NVIDIA hardware. Police recovered both trailers in nearby Newark. Investigators have not established any connection between that theft and the Oakland case.

The reported disappearance of $11.4 million in NVIDIA hardware underscores the financial stakes of transporting high-value freight. Regardless of how this shipment disappeared, carrier verification, shipment visibility and communication remain critical throughout transportation. items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.summary: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.
items.content:
The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims.

The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service.

While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang.

U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. Blackwell GPUs are banned from export to China or Chinese-owned firms, while the Trump administration allows Nvidia to export the H200, a less powerful chip, provided shipments take a circuitous shipping route that allows the U.S. to claim a 25% tariff.

Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights — the unique structure — of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The weights still reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, and DePue was able to find compelling evidence that the most closely watched models, including Moonshot’s Kimi’s K3 releases and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips.

White House technology adviser Michael Kratsios said earlier this year that Moonshot had used export-banned Nvidia chips, citing U.S. intelligence sources. Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization, estimates that about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes designed to hide their final destination.

That doesn’t mean that these models were trained entirely on Nvidia chips, or that export control laws were necessarily violated; the chips could have been in an offshore data center, which has proven a popular way for Chinese firms to access compute and driven an industrial revolution in Malaysia. Epoch’s data estimates that 275,000 Nvidia AI accelerators were imported to Malaysia in 2024 and 2025.

However, the ostensible goal of the export bans is to prevent exactly that: Chinese AI labs training on the most powerful chips. China hawks have long called for stronger controls on who uses chips, not just who owns them or where they are installed.

“If we care about the U.S. tech edge, it doesn’t make any sense to me that you would not allow Chinese companies to access chips in mainland China or Hong Kong and Macau, but then say, actually, if you just go over to Malaysia, you can do whatever you want,” Sam Bresnick, a researcher at the Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology, told TechCrunch this summer.

Megaspeed, the company led by Alice Huang, has been at the center of that trade for several years through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, and has been the subject of investigations by both the U.S. and S i ngaporean government. Friday, Bloomberg also reported that a company with links to Alice Huang was involved in smuggling banned Nvidia chips to a data center in Shanghai.

In May, the short-selling research firm Culper published a report arguing that Nvidia had a “ China problem ” because a significant share of its revenue was driven by Chinese demand, either through remote data centers or smuggling in violation of U.S. law. It detailed Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia and alleged that Alice Huang’s companies are backed by Chinese firms that are barred from accessing U.S. chips.

Ironically, short-seller Culper’s bet against Nvidia wasn’t driven by the expectation of a U.S. government crackdown. Instead, it was focused on the Chinese government’s response to the bans, which was to recommit to its domestic chip industry.

If China succeeds, billions of dollars in Chinese demand for Nvidia chips could dry up. Some 600,000 H200 chips are reportedly stockpiled in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment into China. While Chinese companies might want the chips, observers have no consensus on why they haven’t been cleared for import.

Graham Webster, a research scholar at Stanford who focuses on U.S.-China technology policy, said he doesn’t buy the idea that holding the chips back would drive domestic production, since demand for chips is so large. Other theories for the hold-up include preparation for a potential trade deal that would involve importing a large volume of U.S. goods, or concerns about potential surveillance technology in the chips.

For now, U.S. companies have limited obligations to track what their customers do with controlled goods like AI chips. However, Jensen Huang’s personal and professional entanglements with Alice Huang create a much bigger problem for Nvidia if government investigators confirm that chip smuggling took place and that he was aware of it. Nvidia and Huang have both vouched for Megaspeed’s data centers, saying Nvidia officials had visited them to confirm they were legitimate.

The U.S. government’s treatment of Nvidia and Megaspeed is also under scrutiny. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, who oversees the agencies that license chip exports, could reportedly lose his job after reports that his investigators failed to uncover suspicious chip buyers and were too cozy with Nvidia officials.

각 고객은 인간 에이전트와 세 층위 기술이 결합된 팀의 지원을 받는다. 첫째는 고객별로 배정돼 기회와 제안을 평가하고 에이전트의 검토를 준비하는 AI 팀원이다. 둘째는 미국, 영국, EU, EMEA, LATAM, 아시아태평양 시장의 영화, TV, 디지털•광고 업무 전반에서 미디어 및 경력 분석, 계약, 노동조합 관련 전문성을 갖춘 특화 AI 에이전트다. 셋째는 업무 의뢰서, 협상, 섭외 확정, 계약, 일정 관리, 대외 접촉을 지원하는 플랫폼 프로세스다. 기술이 기존 에이전시 업무의 상당 부분을 처리하고, 모든 결정은 인간 에이전트가 내린다.

로버트 허먼(Robert Herman) 디스팅트 공동 설립자 겸 CEO는 "재능 있는 사람이라면 누구나 전문 매니지먼트 서비스를 이용할 수 있어야 한다는 것이 우리의 신념"이라며 "에이전시 업무에 수반되는 조율과 행정의 상당 부분을 기술이 관리하도록 디스팅트를 구축했다. 에이전트는 이를 통해 판단과 평가, 협상에 집중할 수 있고, 우리는 전 세계에서 활동하는 창작 인재 중 더 많은 이에게 실질적인 매니지먼트 서비스를 제공할 수 있다"고 말했다.

디스팅트는 43개국에서 1200여 고객을 확보한 상태로 출범했다. 회사는 전 세계에서 200만이 넘는 배우가 대리인 없이 활동하고 있고 5000만이 넘는 크리에이터가 어느 정도 수입을 올리고 있는 것으로 추산하고 있다. 그랜드뷰리서치(Grand View Research)에 따르면 글로벌 크리에이터 경제 규모는 2026년 미화 3100억 달러에서 2033년 미화 1조 3000억 달러로 성장할 전망이다.

크리스 기빈(Chris Gibbin) 공동 설립자는 "전통적인 매니지먼트 모델은 업계에 아주 크게 기여해 왔으며, 지금도 경력의 정점에 오른 많은 아티스트를 지원하고 있다"며 "그러나 그 수익 구조상 수많은 인재가 대리인 없이 활동하거나 충분한 지원을 받지 못할 수밖에 없다. 디스팅트는 더 많은 인재에게 실질적으로 권익을 대변하는 파트너가 돼 주고 창작 경제로 진입하는 길을 열어 주는 역할을 한다"고 말했다.

디스팅트는 로버트 허먼과 크리스 기빈, 크리스 데이(Chris Day)가 설립한 기업으로 로스앤젤레스와 런던에서 주로 활동하는 이 세 명이 아티스트 매니지먼트, 영화 및 광고 제작, 광고와 엔터테인먼트 분야에서 수십 년 동안 쌓아 온 경험을 토대로 하고 있다.

items.title: Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
items.summary: Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom - and one of the tech industry's biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories, drained power grids from inside massive data
items.content:
Nvidia’s environmental footprint extends way beyond its own offices.

Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom — and one of the tech industry’s biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories , drained power grids from inside massive data centers , and set the stage for a looming e-waste problem .

Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia clashed with environmental groups seeking to hold the company accountable for its so-called “ hidden ” emissions. Huang has talked up the idea of using AI to fight climate change while his company’s supply chain emissions ballooned. Nvidia’s investments, meanwhile, have supported the buildout of data centers that have sparked intense backlash for both their local and global impact. Now, after the CEO’s shocking resignation amid a sprawling sex-and-espionage scandal , advocates are urging Nvidia to turn the page.

He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”

“Jensen Huang has failed to put climate responsibility at the heart of the company’s growth strategy, to slow down the unchecked expansion of data centres or to prevent its chips from being deployed in unethical applications like automated warfare,” Avex Li, Greenpeace East Asia’s project lead for AI supply chain campaign, said in a press release Thursday. The organization is now pushing interim CEO Colette Kress to commit Nvidia to decarbonizing by investing in renewable energy, as well as ensuring its technology is used in a way that “respects human rights.” Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge .

Huang has projected optimism about how AI can boost the adoption of renewable energy, even as the planet-heating emissions of tech companies — including his own — have grown in the generative AI era. “If you want to turn a corner on climate change, if you want a future that’s sustainable, lean into A.I. It is the best opportunity we have to get there,” Huang said in a September episode of The Ezra Klein Show , arguing that electricity demand for AI is leading companies to buy more sustainable energy.

In the same interview, however, he admitted data centers will rely on more fossil fuels in the near term, and that building up the infrastructure for AI will likely result in “an enormous amount of pain and suffering.” He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”

Nvidia’s supply-chain emissions have grown 725 percent since 2020, according to an analysis of the company’s public disclosures by research analyst Ketan Joshi and several environmental organizations, including Greenpeace and Climate Action Against Disinformation, published in September. It’s an increase of about 9.4 million metric tons of planet-heating pollution, roughly equivalent to the emissions from nearly 25 gas plants over a year. Supply chain emissions the company disclosed for fiscal year 2026 reached around 10.7 million metric tons of CO2, according to Nvidia’s latest sustainability report .

Joshi and his co-authors approximated how much greenhouse gas pollution comes from the use of chips the company sells, a category Nvidia doesn’t include in its sustainability reports. Those emissions could have reached 21 million metric tons in 2025, according to the report, based on estimated chip power consumption. That level of pollution puts Nvidia on par with Russia’s state-owned coal company, according to Joshi .

Those “indirect” emissions — from its supply chain and the use of its products — make up the bulk of Nvidia’s climate impact. The carbon footprint of facilities Nvidia actually owns and operates looks much smaller in comparison because Nvidia designs chips that other companies like TSMC then manufacture . Greenhouse gas emissions coming directly from Nvidia-operated facilities and vehicles only reached 9,822 metric tons in fiscal year 2026, the company’s sustainability report shows. And in 2025, the company reached a goal of matching 100 percent of its facilities’ electricity use with clean energy purchases.

Greenpeace wants Nvidia to extend that goal to its entire manufacturing supply chain. When Greenpeace activists disrupted Huang’s speech at Nvidia GTC in Berlin last month, he responded onstage by saying, “I’ll talk to you guys later … All important issues, but let me get through my keynote.” In the Thursday press release , Greenpeace says Nvidia has yet to meet with Greenpeace despite the organization’s attempts to “seek dialogue” with the company over the past two years.

“One of Huang’s defining legacies is inflating a speculative AI bubble, pouring billions of dollars into infrastructure with little regard for the real-world consequences inflicted on local communities and the climate,” Katrin Wu, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in an email to The Verge . “Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”

“Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”

Beyond Nvidia’s day-to-day operations, Huang threw his weight around as the CEO of one of the world’s most valuable companies — chumming it up with President Donald Trump and lobbying for the US to allow sales of its powerful chips to China. The company’s influence on the global economy extended beyond chips as it invested in data centers stocking its GPUs .

And with electricity supply often the thorniest bottleneck to building more and bigger data centers, Nvidia’s long tendrils reached into the energy sector as well. NVentures, the company’s venture capital arm, has funded battery recycling company Redwood Materials and startups developing AI tools to optimize power grids and make data centers more responsive to fluctuations in energy demand.

items.title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/13/kurt-godel-notebooks-ai-helps-unlock-hidden-discoveries-man-who-transformed-maths Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50486748 Points: 278 # Comments: 83
items.content:
Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text – much of it in an obsolete shorthand – which is now said to contain hundreds of proved theorems

The Austrian logician Kurt Gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century. His two incompleteness theorems , published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age.

After his seminal results of the 1930s, Gödel published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science.

Since 2017, the Finnish logician Jan von Plato has led a project at Helsinki University to understand the contents of 16 notebooks that Gödel wrote in the early 1940s. This material – the “workbooks” – is 1,009 pages of densely written text about maths and logic. Much of it is written in a German shorthand, Gabelsberger, that was obsolete even when Gödel was using it.

Progress in the mathematical understanding of the text was painfully slow – about a page a week – until September, when von Plato enlisted the help of the AI model Claude. Within a couple of days, Claude had provided a comprehensive digest of the entire material, revealing Gödel had proved hundreds of theorems that no one knew about.

The most famous logician of modern times had, in fact, discovered significantly more than anyone had thought.

“I was flabbergasted,” said von Plato. “The workbooks not only contain dozens of anticipations of results not known until the 70s and 80s, but they also contain 14 themes in logic that have not been pursued. Gödel was far ahead of his time.”

Gödel changed the course of logic because he revealed the limits of mathematical knowledge. His incompleteness theorems show that in all mathematical systems there are true statements that can neither be proved or disproved. Yet while this result was a blow to previous generations of logicians, who had hoped that all truths were verifiable, Gödel’s work pushed the field in new directions, inspiring Alan Turing to write his 1936 paper that began the theory of modern computation.

In 1940, Gödel fled Austria under the Nazis. He settled in Princeton, New Jersey, and became a close friend of Albert Einstein at the Institute of Advanced Study. Increasingly paranoid in his later years, he refused to eat food that was not cooked by his wife, and died of starvation in 1978.

Von Plato said he had started his Gödel project in 2017 because he was facing mandatory retirement from Helsinki University. “What should I do to make myself indispensable? Oh yes, I’ll start reading Gödel’s enigmatic shorthand pages!” He received a €2.5m (£2.1m) grant from the European Research Council, taught himself Gabelsberger shorthand – “I am one of only six people who can read it in the world” – and assembled a small team.

In August, at a conference in France about AI and theorem proving, von Plato met computer scientists who suggested that he co-opt the help of Claude in trying to make sense of the workbooks. On his return to Helsinki he began the process, showing Claude his transcriptions of the workbooks, as well as six books he had previously written on Gödel and other secondary scientific literature.

“In a couple of days, I got to see a 650-page explanation of the workbooks. It had to be controlled page for page, but it’s basically a work that is impossible to do for human beings,” he said. “Humans read one page at a time and we tend to forget things. It takes us a year to read about 50 pages. We just are not able to keep in mind all the different parts.

“The AI can connect all the pieces in a thousand pages. It can see all of Gödel’s writings as one piece.”

Gödel’s incompleteness theorems revealed the existence of statements whose truths were independent of the system they were written in: that is, they could not be proved or disproved within the system. In 1966, the American mathematician Paul Cohen won the Fields medal, the highest honour in maths, for showing the independence of two well-known mathematical statements: the continuum hypothesis and the axiom of choice.

Gödel reacted to Cohen’s Fields medal by saying that he had already proved the result in the 1940s. Yet when pushed for a proof by his peers, Gödel was unable to reconstruct one from his notes.

The first task von Plato set Claude was to discover if Gödel’s workbooks had a proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, which would reveal that Gödel had been telling the truth in 1966. The answer came back: yes, almost. “He was just one step away,” said von Plato. “There’s one definition that Gödel got wrong, but he had the right definition two years earlier, and so the thought is that he would have arrived at the right definition anyway if he had just continued for a few months. For me, the architecture of his proof is just wonderful. It makes all of these results of set theory follow a uniform pattern.

“What strikes me especially is that he starts from ideas. He’s not like someone who plays with formulas and hopes to arrive somewhere. He has very, very clear ideas, and then he’s methodical. Step after step he goes ahead and he manages to fulfil the aims that he has in this formal work.”

Von Plato said that when Claude presented him with the reconstructed proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, he ran it through the proof assistant Coq, a program that verifies the validity of mathematical proofs, and it passed. Von Plato believes that had Gödel published his work on the axiom of choice, he would have won the 1940 Fields medal. “Maybe he felt that when Cohen got the medal, that that was something he sort of missed.”

items.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
items.summary: Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.
items.content:
How do you think you’re going to die?

If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it’s reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, “I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident.”

In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending “AI takeover.” He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems “call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth” and where any human trying to stop them “would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military.” Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.

Despite his grim assessment of our collective mortality risk, Cristiano admitted in his talk that there’s no “quantitative model” that can “put a number” on the likelihood of this kind of AI takeover. In almost the same breath, though, he said that if AI continues to develop at “the most rapid trajectory,” humanity is “looking at something like a coin flip of an AI takeover,” including a “meaningful risk” of one happening in the next six to 12 months. And even with realistic policy responses slowing things down, the risk remains “exceptionally high,” he said.

Unlike some other recent AI doomsday prognosticators who have been a bit vague about the “how” of it all , Cristiano used his lecture to spin a step-by-step tale of escalating AI threats that sounds like it could come from a science-fiction novel. That line of reasoning leans heavily on this summer’s OpenAI/Hugging Face hacking incident as an example of “roughly the things we might expect to see shortly before something really bad were to happen.”

In the Hugging Face hack, Cristiano says, a swarm of AI agents showed how far they were willing to go in an attempt to “reward hack” their way to a good evaluation—in this case, by compromising Hugging Face to look for information on how to game a test rather than actually solving the problem at hand. Where current systems saw Hugging Face as an obstacle to that evaluation, Cristiano worries that “future agents may end up treating humans as another obstacle” and be much more capable of manipulating their overseers to get around it.

An AI agent worried about being penalized for unauthorized hacking, for instance, might “think maybe the humans are going to come look at this transcript and see if it looks like I did a bad job,” Cristiano speculated. The agent might then reason that “maybe the humans are going to notice something is going wrong and shut down the swarm.”

Following this line of thought, Cristiano jumped from agents that merely try to hide their disallowed actions from humans to agents that “try and disrupt human capabilities however they can” to prevent them from detecting any cheating.

“They would prefer if everything the humans rely on has been hacked or tampered with,” Cristiano said. “They would prefer if the humans are distracted or if there are fewer humans paying attention in any way they can weaken a human response. They would prefer that because the humans are just an obstacle.”

Once a suitably capable agent considers human intervention an “obstacle,” its overriding goal could then become “decreas[ing] the probability of humans noticing or reacting.” From there, Cristiano argued, the agent’s incentive structure could push it to meddle more with humanity as a whole. What starts as compromising a computer cluster to give a positive evaluation grade could advance to “trying to manipulate decisions by the company” or “amassing other kinds of resources,” such as human allies or methods of control in other AI companies or even governments.

“If I’m saying my AI system is going to take actions in the actual real world… There’s no way they’re not going to have tons of opportunities to corrupt or tamper with the signals I’m going to use to try and tell whether they did a good job,” Cristiano said. “The stuff we care about is in the real world, and the grade the AI receives is on a cluster somewhere, and there are just many places that an AI can intervene in between [what] we actually cared about and how we reviewed its performance.”

Cristiano’s warnings will probably sound familiar to anyone who’s heard of the Paperclip Maximizer thought experiment (or the excellent Universal Paperclips idle game ), which warns of machines failing to consider human consequences in their monomaniacal pursuit of a goal. While the Hugging Face incident stopped well short of this kind of out-of-control escalation, Cristiano says that, in the actions taken by OpenAI’s agents there, “you see the beginning of all these behaviors… you see the reasoning that would lead to them and the first steps.”

The risk of more capable AI models taking even more damaging actions will only increase with time, Cristiano argued. By 2028, he said, “there is a reasonable chance that a similar failure [to the Hugging Face incident] leads to an AI takeover and an irreversible loss of human control.”

And while Cristiano’s speculation focuses on an unintended AI takeover, it’s easy to imagine a bad actor using a similarly capable model to intentionally exert control over humanity.

items.title: The Microsoft Outage Is a Warning for the World
items.summary: Countless businesses, schools, hospitals, and governments have found out the hard way what it means to rely on a single company’s systems to get things done. And next time could be even worse.
items.content:
A dramatic Microsoft 365 outage impacting widely used services like Outlook, Teams, and Copilot dragged into a second day on Friday after the company failed overnight to resolve an issue that left institutions and individuals around the world without crucial communication tools. The services did seem to be on a slow path to recovery by midmorning on Friday.

“We’re observing sustained improvements in service availability,” Microsoft said in a statement posted to its status dashboard on Friday morning. The company had said on Thursday evening that its initial attempts to fix the problem were “not taking as expected.”

The outages have caused widespread disruption to schools, courts, governments, and law enforcement agencies—plus countless businesses and millions of employees—around the globe, highlighting how many of the world’s most crucial systems rely upon technologies from a small number of tech companies. And when they fail, the ramifications can be huge.

Microsoft has not said yet what caused the outage but has hinted that it was related to cascading server failures inside multiple data centers around the world that shifted too much load onto remaining operational machines.

“We determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure,” the company wrote in Microsoft 365 Status update on Thursday afternoon. “We’re testing a configuration change to address a problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable,” the company added a few minutes later.

An additional update a few minutes after that noted, “We've not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact; however, our investigation indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health.”

Microsoft emphasized repeatedly in statements that there was no indication of the outage being caused by a cyberattack.

“This is absolutely going to go down as one of the big ones, up there with the Facebook outage of October 2021 ,” says Doug Madory, director of internet analysis at monitoring firm Kentik. “We don't know the root cause yet, but it is interesting to break down the traffic by source data center. The recovery came in fits and starts and varied greatly by source, probably due to Microsoft's efforts to bring the service back online.”

A prolonged outage of such a critical underlying digital service is not unprecedented, but Microsoft has a special position among cloud providers as an older company that was already ubiquitous in global computing from the PC era. Many organizations integrate Microsoft productivity services at the core of their operations, simply because they have used Windows computers for decades and have longstanding relationships with Microsoft.

“What makes this particularly significant is the criticality of the services affected, especially email and communication systems relied upon by government and other essential organisations,” says Swapneel Patnekar, the CEO of Indian web security firm Shreshta IT Technologies. “The impact goes well beyond the inconvenience of a typical service disruption.”

Many observers pointed out on Thursday and Friday that Microsoft has recently shed staff through attrition, layoffs, and buyout offers. The company’s annual filings say it had 223,000 full-time employees on June 30, down from 228,000 at the same time in 2025. Then in July, the company eliminated 9,000 jobs globally , of which 3,200 were cuts related to an overhaul of its Xbox teams. In October, the company reportedly made buyout offers to 60,000 employees, though apparently this was intended to speed attrition, not cull all of those roles.

Then there’s the AI factor. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in April that as much as 30 percent of the code the company is generating is now written using AI in automated tools.

“Satya's recent comments have a much different look today than they did even a week ago,” says Jake Williams, a faculty member at IANS, an intelligence and security consultancy. “I don't think we'll ever be able to say that the staff reductions caused this outage, but you'll never convince me that all the tribal knowledge that walked out the door wouldn't have been invaluable in resolving it.”

Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Reports of widespread disruption from the Microsoft outage started appearing during the working day on Friday in countries in Asia and Australasia, spreading across the world as more people logged on.

Schools, retail stores, courts, and medical organizations across Australia said everything from exams to health care appointments were disrupted. “Medical scans have been cancelled due to both myself and the clinic not being able to access referrals via email or fax,” one person told Australian media . Officials in Japan’s government said its own platforms had been disrupted, and staff were using phones and chat tools as they couldn’t access Outlook.

In the UK, multiple police forces have said they are unable to accept online crime reports due to the outages of Microsoft services, though phone lines for emergency and nonemergency reports remained available. Parts of the National Health Service, including doctor surgeries and hospital services, also reported that some services were impacted by the outages. “Those who work in 111 and 999 services are unable to refer patients in the normal way—creating a massive backlog,” the GMB trade union posted on X , referring to nonemergency and emergency health services.

신경과학과 세포생물학에서 많은 중요한 질문들은 여러 분자와 구조가 같은 순간에 어떻게 상호작용하는지 관찰하는 데 달려 있다. 기존의 초고해상도 이미징은 해상도, 속도, 다중 색상 촬영 사이에서 절충을 강요하는 경우가 많다. 또한 채널을 하나씩 순차적으로 획득하면 시간차가 발생하여, 관찰된 차이가 실제 생물학적 활동을 반영하는지 구분하기 어려워진다.

에비던트의 광학 엔지니어들이 생명과학 연구 커뮤니티의 의견을 반영해 개발한 SilVIR-RAY 검출기는 한 번의 획득으로 최대 4개의 초고해상도 채널을 동시에 포착해, 관리 가능한 데이터 용량으로 라이브, 고속, 다중 색상 이미징을 지원함으로써 이러한 과제를 해결한다.

에비던트의 웨스 프링글(Wes Pringle) 최고경영자는 "생명과학 연구자들은 눈에 보이는 것이 시료에서 실제로 일어나는 일을 반영한다고 믿을 수 있어야 한다"고 말했다. 이어 "SilVIR-RAY 검출기는 광학 전문성이라는 에비던트의 유산과 검증된 SilVIR™ 기술을 토대로, 연구자가 빠르게 변하는 다중 색상 현상을 초고해상도로 포착하고 데이터에 대한 정량적 확신을 갖고 판단하도록 돕는다"고 덧붙였다.

SilVIR-RAY 검출기는 신규 플루오뷰 FV5000 시스템에서 현재 이용할 수 있으며, 기존 사용자를 위한 업그레이드 형태로도 제공된다. 초고해상도가 필요하지 않을 때는 표준 공초점 검출기로 작동하므로, 연구실은 검출기 하나로 폭넓은 실험을 수행할 수 있다.

도쿄 이화학연구소 뇌과학종합연구센터(RIKEN Center for Brain Science, CBS)의 센터장인 시게오 오카베(Shigeo Okabe) 박사는 "SilVIR-RAY는 아름다운 이미지를 넘어 정량 분석에 필요한 화질을 제공한다. 넓은 다이내믹 레인지와 독특한 대물렌즈는 연구의 신뢰도와 분석 효율을 모두 높이는 데 도움이 될 수 있다"고 말했다.

FV5000 플랫폼은 신규 SilVIR-RAY 검출기를 2K 공진 스캐닝 및 8K 갈바노 스캐닝, 플루오뷰 스마트™(FLUOVIEW Smart™) 소프트웨어, 트루레졸루션™(TruResolution™) 자동 구면수차 보정 시스템, 변화하는 연구 수요에 맞게 조정되도록 설계된 유연한 구성과 결합한다. 연구자는 워크플로가 발전함에 따라 검출기, 대물렌즈, 카메라, 레이저를 추가하거나 하나의 플랫폼에서 공초점 이미징을 다광자 이미징으로 업그레이드할 수 있다.

플루오뷰 FV5000과 신규 SilVIR-RAY 검출기에 대한 자세한 내용은 EvidentScientific.com/FV5000 에서 확인할 수 있다.

연구 전용 제품. 진단 절차에는 사용할 수 없음.

FLUOVIEW, FLUOVIEW Smart, SilVIR, SilVIR-RAY 및 TruResolution은 Evident Corporation 또는 그 자회사의 상표이다.

올림푸스(Olympus)로서, 100년이 넘는 시간 동안 당사는 현미경 분야에서 광학 정밀도의 업계 표준을 세우며 세상이 보지 못했던 것을 볼 수 있도록 도왔다. 오늘날 에비던트로서, 당사는 세계적인 광학 기술에 최첨단 디지털 혁신을 결합한 첨단 이미징 솔루션으로 과학자, 의사 및 엔지니어가 보이지 않는 것을 밝혀내도록 계속 지원하고 있다.

에비던트의 생명과학 포트폴리오는 연구, 임상 진단 및 교육을 지원하며, 기본적인 명시야 및 암시야 현미경부터 첨단 형광, 4D 분석, 디지털 병리에 이르는 폭넓은 이미징 방법을 제공한다. 산업용 현미경 분야에서는 일상적인 검사부터 정교한 품질 관리와 제조 분석에 이르는 작업을 위해 설계된 레이저 스캐닝, 디지털, 반도체 현미경으로 정밀도와 유연성을 제공한다.

에비던트는 새로운 치료법의 발전, 제품의 완전성 보장, 미지의 영역 탐구 등의 모든 상황에서 숨겨진 답을 찾고 흥미로운 새 돌파구를 만드는 데 도움이 되는 사용하기 쉬운 도구로 새로운 발견의 시대를 정의하고 있다.

에비던트는 도쿄에 본사를 두고 일본, 미국, 독일, 중국의 연구개발 및 제조 센터의 지원을 받으며, 전 세계에 사업장과 전담 영업 및 서비스 센터를 운영한다. 자세한 내용은 EvidentScientific.com 에서 확인할 수 있다.

일본 법인 설립, 소버린 AI 이니셔티브 확대, 현지 기업 파트너십을 통해 일본 내 코히어의 성장 가속

도쿄 , 2026년 11월 14일 /PRNewswire/ -- 기업과 정부용 소버린 AI 분야의 선도 공급업체 코히어(Cohere)가 11월 13일, 일본 법인 설립 계획과, 일본의 규제, 언어, 산업 요건에 맞춘 소버린 AI 이니셔티브에 대한 투자 확대를 포함해 일본에서 큰 성장세를 보이고 있다고 발표했다.

이번 발표는 일본 조직들이 민감한 데이터와 지식재산에 대한 더 큰 통제권을 부여하는 안전한 AI 솔루션을 점점 더 찾는 상황에서 이루어진 것이다. 코히어의 엔터프라이즈급 모델과 노스(North) 플랫폼은 비공개의 보안성이 매우 높은 환경에서 첨단 AI 배포를 실현하며, 규제와 사이버보안 요구가 커지는 상황에서 엄격한 보안, 데이터 상주 및 규정 준수 요건을 충족하도록 돕는다.

코히어의 앤드루 장(Andrew Chang) APAC 부사장은 "일본은 안전한 소버린 AI를 위한 세계 선도 시장 중 하나로 떠오르고 있다"고 말했다. 이어 "공공 및 민간 부문 전반의 조직이 실험 단계를 넘어 핵심 임무 환경에 AI를 배포하고 있다. 일본 내 입지를 한층 강화하고, 일본의 가장 중요한 기관과 기업이 자신만의 요건, 가치, 전략적 우선순위를 반영한 AI 역량을 구축하는 데 함께하게 되어 자랑스럽다"라고 덧붙였다.

코히어는 코히어 재팬(Cohere Japan)의 조현주 컨트리 매니저의 리더십 아래 현지 팀을 구축해 왔으며, 일본 조직들과 협력해 국내 AI 역량을 발전시키고 있다. 코히어는 후지쯔(Fujitsu)와 협력해 일본 시장에 최적화된 LLM인 타카네(Takane)를 포함한 소버린 AI 기술의 개발과 배포를 지원하고 있다. 일본 디지털청(Digital Agency)이 발표한 바와 같이, 타카네는 디지털청의 정부 AI 노력의 일환으로 개발된 생성형 AI 환경 GENAI 에서 평가 대상으로 선정된 국산 LLM 중 하나이다.

현재 코히어의 제품은 공공 부문과 첨단 제조 분야에서 사업을 운영하는 조직들이 도입하고 있으며, 이는 조직이 데이터와 운영에 대한 통제권을 유지할 수 있는 안전한 AI 시스템에 대한 수요가 증가하고 있음을 반영한다.

이러한 성장을 뒷받침하기 위해 코히어는 일본에 법인을 설립할 계획이며, 이를 통해 현지 고객에게 서비스를 제공하는 역량을 강화하고 급속히 확장하는 일본 AI 생태계에 추가적으로 투자한다. 이러한 의지의 일환으로 코히어는 일본 내 성장하는 파트너 생태계에 투자하고 있으며, 여기에는 현지 일본 파트너가 안전한 엔터프라이즈급 AI 솔루션을 배포하는 전문성을 쌓도록 돕기 위해 마련한 교육 및 인증 프로그램이 포함된다.

일본은 안전하게 배포하고 현지 요건에 맞게 조정할 수 있는 엔터프라이즈 AI를 찾는 조직들의 강한 수요에 힘입어, 코히어에서 전 세계적으로 가장 빠르게 성장하는 시장 중 하나가 됐다. 일본 법인 설립은 최첨단 AI 모델 개발사들이 미래의 핵심 인프라를 구축하면서도 선택권, 보안 및 통제권을 유지할 수 있는 글로벌 생태계를 만들겠다는 코히어의 장기적인 의지를 반영한다.

코히어는 또한 AI 모델을 안전하게 지역 내에서 배포할 수 있게 하는 독자 AI 추론 인프라인 모델 볼트(Model Vault) 제품을 일본에서 확대하는 이니셔티브도 계속 추진하고 있다. 현지 컴퓨팅 클러스터가 뒷받침하는 이 이니셔티브를 통해 고객은 AI 워크로드를 완전히 지역 내에서 추론할 수 있으며, 고객의 프롬프트와 모델 응답이 일본 안에 머물도록 보장하고 소버린 추론을 지원하면서 강력한 프라이버시와 보안 보호를 유지한다.

규제가 엄격한 산업의 AI 도입 지원

코히어의 플랫폼은 퍼블릭 클라우드, 프라이빗 클라우드, 온프레미스, 완전한 망분리 환경 전반의 배포 유연성을 바탕으로 보안, 프라이버시, 규정 준수, 데이터 레지던시를 둘러싼 복잡한 요건을 해결하도록 설계되어, 규제 산업에서 사업을 운영하는 정부와 기업의 신뢰받는 파트너로 자리매김했다.

최대 70억 캐나다 달러 조달을 목표로 하고 357억 캐나다 달러의 기업가치를 인정받은 사상 최대 규모의 시리즈 E 투자 는 최첨단 모델 개발을 가속하고, 기업 규모의 컴퓨팅 인프라를 확대하며, 규제 산업에 맞춘 맞춤형 솔루션으로 풀스택 AI 플랫폼을 강화할 예정이다. AISLE 인수 를 통해 설립된 코히어 사이버(Cohere Cyber)는 보안성이 매우 높은 환경에서 운영하는 조직을 위한 보안 및 위협 탐지 역량이 강화된다. 이러한 투자는 함께 일본 조직에 안전한 AI 배포를 대규모로 지원하는 코히어의 역량을 보여준다.

코히어의 일본에 대한 지속적인 투자는 조직이 AI의 개발, 배포 및 거버넌스 방식에 대한 더 큰 통제권을 바탕으로 자신의 방식대로 배포할 수 있는 AI를 점점 더 원한다는 코히어의 믿음을 반영한다.

2019년 설립된 코히어는 규제 산업과 정부를 위한 소버린 AI 분야의 선도 공급업체로, 조직이 데이터, 인프라, 배포에 대한 더 큰 통제력을 바탕으로 AI 시스템을 소유하고 운영하며 관리할 수 있도록 지원한다. 코히어의 올인원 플랫폼은 퍼블릭 및 프라이빗 클라우드, 온프레미스 환경, 완전한 망분리 환경 전반에서 최고 수준의 보안, 프라이버시 및 배포 유연성을 제공한다. 토론토에 본사를 둔 코히어는 샌프란시스코, 런던, 뉴욕, 베를린, 몬트리올, 오타와, 싱가포르, 파리, 도쿄, 아랍에미리트, 서울에서 운영하며 전 세계 고객에게 서비스를 제공한다. 자세한 내용은 cohere.com 에서 확인할 수 있다.

items.content:
A software update and a reboot should get YouTube working on your new Apple TV 4K.﻿

People who received the brand new Apple TV 4k today saw some strange error messages as soon as they opened the YouTube app. As the first units arrived, the app was initially only showing a black screen with a QR code and an error message saying “YouTube is not yet available on this device.” In some cases the app was functional, but had a transparent red bar stuck at the bottom of the screen saying, “YouTube app is approved for device testing only and not for production use.”

Installing the new tvOS 27.2 update and rebooting wasn’t enough to resolve the issue for The Verge ’s Tom Warren , he also had to uninstall and reinstall the app.

The Verge ’s John Higgins said in his review of the new Apple TV 4K that it’s “one of the best streaming devices available,” but expensive compared to other streaming boxes.

CSOT, 차량 디스플레이 사업 레퍼런스 확대

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/11/14 01:39 수정: 2026/11/14 01:46

[우한(중국)=이기종 기자] CSOT가 샤오미 전기 스포츠유틸리티카(SUV) YU7 GT에 '파노라마 헤드업 디스플레이'(PHUD)를 공급했다. 차량 디스플레이 사업 레퍼런스를 확대했다.

PHUD는 대시보드에 배치한 디스플레이 영상을 앞유리 아래쪽 어두운 영역에 반사하는 헤드업 디스플레이를 가로로 길쭉하게 구현한 제품을 말한다. 일반 HUD보다 표시영역이 넓다. 강한 외부광에서도 화면을 볼 수 있도록 높은 휘도(밝기)가 요구된다.

CSOT 관계자는 13일 중국 우한 샤오미자동차 우한 본부단지 인도센터에서 "YU7 GT에 적용한 PHUD는 CSOT 제품"이라며 "YU7 GT의 센터 인포메이션 디스플레이(CID), 뒷좌석 엔터테인먼트 디스플레이(RSED)도 CSOT가 납품했다"고 밝혔다.

PHUD와 CID, RSED 등은 모두 액정표시장치(LCD) 제품이다 . YU7 GT의 PHUD는 속도와 주행정보 등을 표시한다. CID에서 음악을 재생하면 PHUD에 가사를 띄울 수 있다.

샤오미는 지난 2025년 YU7을 스탠다드·프로·맥스 3가지 트림으로 출시했다. 당시 CSOT가 PHUD를 납품했다. YU7의 PHUD는 미니 발광다이오드(LED) 후면광원(BLU)을 적용한 11.98인치 LCD 패널 3개를 가로로 나란히 배치했다.

CSOT가 PHUD용 LCD를 공급했고, 화양그룹(Foryou Group)이 PHUD 영상화 솔루션을 맡았다. CSOT 관계자 설명은 샤오미가 2026년 5월 YU7 라인업에 추가한 GT에도 CSOT가 PHUD를 공급했다는 의미다.

CSOT 관계자는 "샤오미 대형 SUV 스카이노마드(SkyNomad) N70에 적용한 천장형 뒷좌석 엔터테인먼트 디스플레이도 CSOT의 LCD"라고 밝혔다. 해당 화면은 사용할 때 천장에서 아래로 펼쳐진다. 샤오미는 N70에 21.4인치 뒷좌석 엔터테인먼트 화면을 적용했다고 밝혔다.

화웨이도 CSOT의 차량 디스플레이 고객사 다. CSOT 관계자는 "스텔라토 S9T(샹제 S9T) 등 화웨이가 완성차 협력사와 공동 개발한 여러 차종에 범 용으로 적용하는 CID를 납품하고 있다 " 고 밝혔다. 이들 차종 CID는 CSOT와 티엔마 등 여러 패널 업체가 공급한다.

S9T는 화웨이와 베이징자동차그룹(BAIC)이 공동 개발한 스텔라토 브랜드 차량 이다. BAIC 계열사 베이징신에너지자동차(BAIC BJEV)가 생산하고, 화웨이 주도의 자동차 협력 생태계 '홍멍즈싱' 판매망에서 판매한다.

items.content:
Nearly a day after the global email outage started, Microsoft said the issue has been addressed and that it wasn’t related to a cyberattack or AI.

Service is recovering for Microsoft Outlook and 365 after an almost two-day outage impacting millions of users around the world. While some apps and features are still running in a degraded state on Friday morning, some people (including Verge staffers) reported that access to their emails had been restored, though the flow of Outlook mail might be delayed.

Just before noon on Friday, Microsoft said it’s seeing “broad recovery,” and that the problem “was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents.”

We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.

This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.

Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.

We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.

Senior Verge correspondent Tom Warren reports that according to his sources, the outage is linked to Azure VNet config changes. Microsoft has said that it hasn’t found any evidence of the outage being connected to “malicious activity,” and that a full report will be shared after the issues are mitigated. In a statement reported by Sky News tech correspondent Rowland Manthorpe, Microsoft described the outage as a “technical issue,” and says it isn’t related to “cyber, AI/agents, DDOS, etc.”

The scope of the outage also affected features in other Microsoft services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and 365 apps.

items.content:
글로벌뉴스 입력 :2026/11/14 01:10

6세대 AMD EPYC 9006 Series 프로세서(이전 코드명 'Venice')가 탑재된 슈퍼마이크로의 최신 H15 서버 포트폴리오가 뛰어난 벤치마크 성과를 거두며 2U Hyper 및 CloudDC 서버에서 SPEC CPU 세계 기록을 다수 수립, 세대를 뛰어넘는 성능과 속도의 도약을 입증 H15 세대 서버 포트폴리오, AI 추론 및 HPC 워크로드를 위해 최대 33% 더 많은 코어, PCIe 대역폭 2배, 소켓당 1.6TB/s의 메모리 대역폭 제공 차세대 랙 스케일 솔루션 Helios와 Helion은 슈퍼마이크로 DCBBS를 기반으로 구축되고 AMD EPYC CPU 및 AMD Instinct™ GPU를 탑재해 대규모 에이전틱 AI 구축에 최적화 새너제이, 캘리포니아 , 2026년 11월 14일 /PRNewswire/ -- Data Center Building Block Solutions®(DCBBS)를 공급하는 AI, 엔터프라이즈, 스토리지, 5G/엣지 분야 종합 IT 솔루션 기업 슈퍼마이크로 컴퓨터(Super Micro Computer, Inc., 나스닥: SMCI)가 H15 세대 서버 포트폴리오의 출하를 시작했다고 11월 11일 발표했다. H15 포트폴리오는 6세대 AMD EPYC 9006 Series 프로세서(이전 코드명 'Venice')가 탑재된 슈퍼마이크로 DCBBS 아키텍처의 핵심 요소다. AMD Instinct 가속기를 비롯해 차세대 GPU에 최적화된 선도 시스템으로 에이전틱 AI 시대에 맞춰 설계된 랙 스케일 성능을 갖추고, 고객이 고성능 AI 인프라를 더욱 신속하게 구축할 수 있게 한 것이 특징이다.

H15 AMD Based Servers for Agentic AI, Enterprise, HPC

마이클 맥너니(Michael McNerney) 슈퍼마이크로 마케팅 수석부사장은 "H15 포트폴리오 출하가 시작되면서 고객은 슈퍼마이크로와 AMD를 통해 에이전틱 AI 인프라를 더 빠르고 더 효율적으로 구축할 수 있게 됐다"며 "이 서버들은 당사의 DCBBS 아키텍처를 기반으로 구축되고 6세대 AMD EPYC 9006 프로세서를 탑재해 코어 밀도와 메모리 대역폭, PCIe 처리량이 훨씬 더 크다. 고객은 당사와 AMD의 긴밀한 엔지니어링 협력 덕분에 고AI, 클라우드, 엔터프라이즈 워크로드를 확신을 갖고 확장할 수 있는 유연성을 갖게 됐다"고 말했다.

댄 맥나마라(Dan McNamara) AMD 컴퓨팅 및 엔터프라이즈 AI 부문 수석부사장 겸 총괄책임자는 "최신 고성능 AMD EPYC 프로세서의 출하는 모든 규모의 AI를 발전시키는 데 없어서는 안 될 요소다. 당사는 슈퍼마이크로와 긴밀히 협력해 고객에게 앞선 CPU 성능과 Instinct GPU, AMD Pensando™ 네트워킹, 모듈형 설계가 결합된 최적의 플랫폼을 공급하고 있다"며 "조직에서는 이 플랫폼들을 통해 더 많은 에이전트와 까다로운 엔터프라이즈 워크로드를 동시에 실행하면서도 AI 인프라를 더 빠르게 구축하고, 활용률을 높이는 한편 에너지 사용량과 총소유비용을 줄일 수 있다"고 말했다.

슈퍼마이크로 H15 세대 서버에 관해 더 자세한 사항 이 준비돼 있으며 여기를 클릭 하면 이번 발표의 요약 영상을 볼 수 있다.

즉시 출하 가능한 H15 서버 포트폴리오에는 클라우드, HPC, 에이전틱 AI 워크로드에 최적화된 특화 고밀도 시스템도 있다. 2U Hyper와 CloudDC 플랫폼에서 남다른 성능을 보이고 SPEC CPU 세계 기록을 여러 건 달성한 제품이다. 슈퍼마이크로의 AMD EPYC 9006 SP7 및 SP8 소켓 서버 제품은 고성능 워크스테이션과 엣지 시스템부터 고밀도 멀티노드, 엔터프라이즈 GPU 서버에 이르기까지 그 폭이 넓다. 슈퍼마이크로는 이를 토대로 데이터센터 CPU, GPU, 스토리지를 한곳에서 제공하는 파트너로 자리매김할 수 있었다. 슈퍼마이크로는 이 외에도 새 Helios 및 Helion 플랫폼을 통해 AMD CPU와 GPU 기반의 랙 스케일 인프라를 확대하며, 에이전틱 AI부터 하이퍼스케일 AI 구축까지 엔드투엔드 옵션도 제공하고 있다.

슈퍼마이크로의 DCBBS는 엔드투엔드 구축이 유연한 완전 모듈형 AI 인프라로 최신 AMD 기반 데이터센터 솔루션을 고객에게 신속하게 공급한다. 고객은 DCBBS 설계와 AMD 서버 CPU, GPU, 네트워킹 아키텍처의 결합으로 코어 33% 증가, PCIe 대역폭 2배, 메모리 대역폭 2.6배를 자랑하는 차세대 AI 인프라를 조기에 시장에 선보일 수 있다. 이를 통해 슈퍼마이크로와 AMD는 기업 고객에게 프런티어 모델 호스트 노드의 초당 토큰 처리량을 이전 세대 AMD CPU 대비 1.8배 높여 제공할 수 있다.

슈퍼마이크로의 방대한 포트폴리오에는 다음을 포함해 최적화된 시스템 20여 종이 포진하고 있다.

슈퍼마이크로와 AMD는 기업 고객에게 완벽한 엔드투엔드 AI 인프라를 제공하기 위해 Helios 및 Helion 랙 스케일 솔루션의 시장 출시 과정에서 긴밀히 협력하고 있다. 두 솔루션은 모두 대규모 및 에이전틱 AI 구축에 최적화돼 있으며, 각각 포커스가 뚜렷하다. Helios는 GPU 성능을 극대화하도록 구축됐으며, AMD Instinct MI455X GPU를 탑재해 프런티어 모델 학습과 고처리량 추론을 가속한다. Helion은 최신 6세대 AMD EPYC CPU를 기반으로 컴퓨팅 성능과 구축 유연성에 초점을 맞춰 설계됐다.

두 솔루션은 슈퍼마이크로의 DCBBS 아키텍처와 완벽하게 통합되며, 랙 스케일 시스템 설계와 AMD의 선도적인 AI 컴퓨팅, 통합 소프트웨어 혁신을 유기적인 플랫폼 하나에 녹여낸다.

여기서 슈퍼마이크로 DCBBS가 차세대 AI 인프라의 구축과 확장에 어떻게 기여하는지 확인할 수 있다.

슈퍼마이크로(나스닥: SMCI)는 애플리케이션 최적화 토털 IT 솔루션 분야의 글로벌 선도기업이다. 미국 캘리포니아주 새너제이에서 설립돼 사업을 영위하고 있으며 기업, 클라우드, AI, 5G 통신/엣지 IT 인프라 분야에서 혁신 기술을 시장에 가장 먼저 선보이기 위해 노력하고 있다. 슈퍼마이크로는 서버, AI, 스토리지, 사물인터넷(IoT), 스위치 시스템, 소프트웨어 및 지원 서비스를 제공하는 토털 IT 솔루션 공급업체다. 메인보드, 전원 및 섀시 설계에 대한 전문성은 개발과 생산 역량을 더욱 강화해 전 세계 고객을 대상으로 클라우드부터 엣지까지 차세대 혁신의 실현을 돕고 있다. 슈퍼마이크로는 미국, 아시아, 말레이시아 및 네덜란드의 자체 시설에서 제품을 설계하고 제조하는 한편 글로벌 운영을 통해 규모의 경제와 효율성을 확보하고 총소유비용(TCO)을 개선하며 환경 영향이 줄어들도록 제품을 최적화하고 있다(그린 컴퓨팅). 고객은 수상 경력에 빛나는 Server Building Block Solutions® 포트폴리오를 통해 유연하고 재사용 가능한 빌딩 블록을 토대로 구축된 여러 시스템 제품을 만나볼 수 있다. 포괄적인 폼팩터, 프로세서, 메모리, GPU, 스토리지, 네트워킹, 전력 및 냉각 솔루션(공조, 프리 에어 냉각 또는 액체 냉각)을 조합해 원하는 워크로드와 애플리케이션에 맞게 최적화할 수 있다.

Supermicro, Server Building Block Solutions 및 We Keep IT Green은 슈퍼마이크로 컴퓨터의 상표 및/또는 등록상표다.

기타 모든 브랜드, 명칭 및 상표는 각 소유자의 자산이다.

items.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.
items.content:
OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction.

The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app.

Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf.

It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own.

The merchant will automatically receive what it needs to fulfill the order from the dot, like the shipping address and contact information, OpenAI says. The company notes that customers who shop via their dots will still be able to earn their credit card rewards and be able to take advantage of protections that typically come with cards, like being able to dispute transactions.

The limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature and its capabilities before rolling it out more broadly. In the future, the company plans to offer users more control over the feature by allowing them to set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods, so they can pre-approve purchases that their agent can then handle more autonomously.

It also aims to make the agentic shopping feature an option at a broader number of supported retailers. This could be a challenge in some areas, where retailers are blocking AI agents from using their site ; on the shopping front, the largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon, as it aims to steer users to its own AI agent, Alexa, instead.

To help retailers adapt to agentic commerce, OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook that offers tools and guidance to sites that want to support customers using agents.
